topic: The Tragedy of Charlie Gordon: Flowers for Algernon
audience: English learners at B1 and above; analytical storytelling with synchronized visual beats and layered motion.
goal: Explain the tragic psychological paradox of Flowers for Algernon: why intelligence alone cannot buy human belonging.

required_points.text: Charlie seeks intelligence because he believes it is the bridge to human acceptance.
The surgery rapidly transforms his intellect, turning him into a genius.
Awareness brings painful realization: his friends were mocking him, not laughing with him.
The tragic paradox reveals that higher intellect built an invisible wall of isolation.
Brilliance can explain the world, but without emotional warmth, it only magnifies loneliness.

tone: Thoughtful, poignant explanatory storytelling with clear causal reasoning and sharp emotional payoff.
style: Hand-drawn 2D explainer illustration in a marker-pen look: thick black outlines, flat muted colors, full-bleed setting backgrounds, clear props and simple annotations (red circles/arrows). No main character, presenter or recurring protagonist: an anonymous stick-figure cast (round white heads, expressive simple faces, stick limbs) whose roles come from scene costume, hair and props.

success_criteria: Viewer understands Charlie's root motivation, the rapid causal chain, the cruel awakening, and the tragic paradox.
Visual beats and layered motion precisely synchronize with key spoken words.
avoid: Superficial plot recap without causal depth
Photorealism, dark cinematic grading, or decorative text
planning.prior_knowledge: B1 English comprehension; narrative causality explains all thematic shifts.
planning.pacing: Causal visual changes following spoken meaning; allow each actual sentence or diagram enough reading time. No fixed cut or image-count quota.
domain_requirements: Narration and learner-facing text are entirely English; explain meaning and narrative causality inside the same situation.
One central question or situation develops through cause, action and consequence and receives a payoff.
Use story shots, close action and diagrams where they prove meaning; preserve camera/background with Base reference for state changes.
Scene/image/beat counts are chosen for this specific script and saved before narration anchors; no universal scene count.

No recurring protagonist, presenter or host: each scene uses only the anonymous stick figures, animals or objects its action needs, identified by costume/props; keep a figure's costume consistent across Base-reference variations.
assumptions: Duration is a planning estimate; use actual collected narration.
Scene count determined by the 5 causal beats.

text_style.outline: High contrast against a bright clear background
text_style.size: Readable on a phone, at most two meaningful caption lines
text_style.placement: Near the referent for teaching text; keep separate from captions
